description.narrative: Development objective: Policy makers in the Kenyan society base their decisions on unbiased, reliable and quality statistics that helps them to design policies that contribute to creating better living conditions for the people of Kenya. Although the project proposal does not says so, this also means that citizens are better informed and can better hold governments accountable. Project objective: Increased access to statistics that meet user needs. This of course implies improved production too. Component 1 - Statistical products Outcome 1: Improved range and quality of statistical products, including gender statistics, the Statistical Business Register, and geospatial statistics. Component 2 - Management Outcome 2.1: Leadership motivates and supports the staff at KNBS to successfully adopt change in order to achieve the organisation's goals (defined in KNBS’s strategy). Outcome 2.2: Management use performance data to continuously assess KNBS’s work and improve the utilization of resources. Component 3 - Quality assurance Outcome 3.1: Statistics are produced using standardised processes. Outcome 3.2: Statistics are sufficiently documented. Component 4 - Information and communication technology Outcome 4.1: Statistics production is done efficiently and securely Outcome 4.2: Efficient tools are used for statistics production and dissemination Component 5 - The Kenya National Statistical System (NSS) Outcome 5.1: KNBS supports and coordinates the “Sector Statistics”, i.e., the NSS’s data producers Outcome 5.2: KNBS provides guidelines and standards to the Sectors Young Statisticians Program, which will train eight people per year over the five-year program for employment at KNBS.

Detta är ett projekt som stöder Kenya National Bureau of Statistics (KNBS) i samarbete med Statistiska centralbyrån (SCB) med SEK 49,8 miljoner år 2022-2026. Det yttersta målet med projektet är att beslutsfattare i det kenyanska samhället baserar sina beslut på opartisk, tillförlitlig och kvalitetsstatistik som hjälper dem att utforma policyer som bidrar till att skapa bättre levnadsvillkor för folket i Kenya. Det specifika målet är att öka tillgången till statistik som tillgodoser användarnas behov.
KNBS och SCB har samarbetat i två tidigare projekt -- insats 51110063 Statistics Support-KNBS (SEK 34,4 miljoner år 2014-2019) och insats 11333 Extensionssamarbete KNBS & SCB (SEK 19,5 miljoner år 2019-2021). Detta stöd har varit mycket framgångsrikt. KNBS har varit aktivt engagerade och tillsammans med SCB har de hanterat de problem som har uppstått effektivt. Stödet utvärderades självständigt 2020 (Frans van Gerwen och Norah Madaya, “Evaluation of Cooperation Between Kenya National Bureau of Statistics and Statistics Sweden since 2014,” Sida Decentralized Evaluation 2021: 4). Utvärderarna bedömde samarbetet som mycket relevant och effektivt för att stärka och konsolidera KNBS och dess produktion av statistikdata och analys för socialekonomisk utveckling i Kenya.
Det främsta argumentet för detta stöd är att det stärker KNBS förmåga att bidra till öppenhet, ansvarsskyldighet och informerad offentlig debatt och till en offentlig sektor som effektivt kan spela sin roll i utveckling och flerdimensionell fattigdomsbekämpning.
Projektet består av fem komponenter: * Specifika statistiska produkter (inklusive genderstatistik, statistiskt företagsregister och geospatial statistik) * Management * Statistisk kvalitetssäkring * Informations- och kommunikationsteknologi * Det kenyanska nationella statistiksystemet och Programmet för yngre statistiker.
Ambassaden på Sidas vägnar ska underteckna ett avtal med SCB och ett annat avtal med det kenyanska finansministeriet (National Treasury) på KNBS vägnar.

This is a project supporting the Kenya National Bureau of Statistics (KNBS) in cooperation with Statistics Sweden (Statistiska centralbyrån, SCB) with SEK 49.8 million 2022-2026. The ultimate objective of the project is that policy makers in the Kenyan society base their decisions on unbiased, reliable and quality statistics that help them to design policies that contribute to creating better living conditions for the people of Kenya. The specific objective is to increase access to statistics that meet user needs.
KNBS and SCB have cooperated in two previous projects – contributions 51110063 Statistics Support-KNBS (SEK 34.4 million 2014-2019) and 11333 Extension cooperation KNBS & Statistics Sweden (SEK 19.5 million 2019-2021). This support has been very successful. KNBS has been actively engaged and together with SCB they have dealt effectively with the problems that have arisen. The support was independently evaluated in 2020 (Frans van Gerwen and Norah Madaya, “Evaluation of Cooperation Between Kenya National Bureau of Statistics and Statistics Sweden Since 2014,” Sida Decentralised Evaluation 2021:4). The evaluators judged the cooperation highly relevant and effective in strengthening and consolidating KNBS and its production of statistics data and analysis for social economic development of Kenya.
The primary argument for this support is that it strengthens KNBS ability to contribute to transparency, accountability and informed public debate and to a public sector that can effectively play its role in development and multi-dimensional poverty reduction.
The project consists of five components: *Specific statistical products (including gender statistics, statistical business register and geospatial statistics) *Management *Statistical quality assurance *Information and communication technology *The Kenyan National Statistical System and the Young Statisticians Program.
The Embassy on behalf of Sida will sign one agreement with SCB and another agreement with the Kenya National Treasury on behalf of KNBS.

description.narrative:
Overall outcomes of the project have substantially grown during 2025 with increased access to statistics that meet user needs. Key achievements span over all five components of the project. Together they reflect both expanded statistical output and stronger institutional capacity to produce, document, and disseminate statistics sustainably. The accumulated progress during the course of the contribution has lead to the KNBS demonstrating growing ownership and capacity to maintain progress independently.
Results from the five project components include:
Component 1 - Statistical products
Outcome 1: Improved range and quality of statistical products
• KNBS improved the range of gender statistics and have implemented sex disaggregated statistics whenever possible. Of particular importance was the launch of the satellite accounts for household production, that was executed together with UN Women. The study measures the amount of unpaid household chores men and women, respectively, do every day. The statistics generated clear and significant engagement from Principal Secretaries in economic planning and gender, who explicitly identified the statistics as essential evidence for designing policies to reduce women's time burden in unpaid work. The work also enables Kenya to report on SDG Indicator 5.4.1, meeting both national and international monitoring needs. • KNBS has signed an MoU with Kenya Revenue Authority (KRA) on sharing administrative business data, enabling a modernisation of the Statistical Business Register (StatBus 2.0). These activities has resulted in a transition from manual, ad-hoc updates to a systematic framework which is continuously updated, and constitutes high-quality sample frame for all business surveys. The register now serves as the backbone of the entire economic statistical system. • Kenya's first Environmental Statistics Report was released in early 2025. Products made in this project on environment statistics will enable Kenya to meet international reporting requirements while providing policymakers with actionable data for designing green growth strategies and evaluating carbon-related policies. • The project achieved a significant breakthrough in trade statistics that culminated in KNBS's commitment to participate in the OECD Trade in Value Added initiative (TiVA). The initiative directly adresses high-priority policy needs.
Component 2 - Management
Outcome 2.1: Leadership motivates and supports the staff at KNBS to successfully adopt change to achieve the organisation's goals (as defined in KNBS' strategy)
KNBS is advancing toward a more modern organisation through several key initiatives by management anchored in the five year strategy, including:
• Investments in a new data science team, strategically integrated with the "Young Statistician Program", opening opportunities to move beyond isolated capacity building to systematic institutional transformation. • Developing the critical infrastructure, advancing work on the ICT strategy and the Open Data Portal 2.0, representing a transformative move away from the PDF files toward machine-readable data dissemination. • Increased focus on quality assurance development. • Demands for of a comprehensive curriculum to enhance and improve the training programs for staff.
Outcome 2.2: Management use performance data to continuously assess KNBSs work and improve the utilization of resources
• During 2025 KNBS implemented a modernisation of both the monitoring system, including a release calendar and reporting, in where punctuality and timeliness are tracked frequently, and monitoring report. This institutionalisation of performance monitoring showcases progress in regards to institutional capacity. • However, punctuality of statistical releases fell back to 40% during 2025 (same as the baseline from 2023), after an improvement during 2024 to almost 60% (compared to the target of 80% by end of project). Although the KNBS management are increasingly focused on this, punctuality remains a challenge. • Three new management information systems has been developed: a data request system to track and categorize public data requests, enabling KNBS to identify patterns and transform frequent requests into official statistical products; a complaints management system to systematically capture and analyse feedback for service improvement; and a risk monitoring system to improve organisational planning and risk mitigation.
Component 3 - Quality assurance
Outcome 3.1: Statistics are produced using standardised processes
• By 2025, documentation of generic statistical processes reached a level of maturity where KNBS no longer requires external support for basic Kenyan Statistical Process Model maintenance. Focused shifted from product-specific documentation to a broader quality and metadatasystem with standardised processes serving not only KNBS but also other NSS producers. • The generic production processes are now thoroughly documented with improved navigation features, visual process diagrams, and automated HTML conversion capabilities. This documentation provides transparency and creates a foundation for efficient resource utilization and knowledge management. • KNBS began developing a comprehensive metadata management system in 2024 which is still not fully implemented. However, progress continued during 2025 and the institutional commitment suggests that this output will be realised during this year.
Outcome 3.2: Statistics are sufficiently documented
• KNBS achieved a transformative milestone in 2025 by establishing a comprehensive documentation ecosystem that makes statistics truly accessible and verifiable for users. • A quality and metadata portal has been established, developed in collaboration with the Young Statisticians program and inspired by Eurostat's Metadata Handler. The portal transforms documentation from scattered PDF files into an integrated, accessible resource. • The narrative report for 2025 suggests that KNBS now possesses both the infrastructure and capacity to maintain comprehensive statistical documentation as standard institutional practice.
Component 4 - Information and communication technology (ICT)
Outcome 4.1: Statistics production is done efficiently and securely
• During 2025 the development of KNBSs ICT strategy continued moving from manual to integrated digital systems. Moreover, a strategic and technical foundation for a modernized domain network was established. • The transition towards a modern storage solution, including cloud-based integration and centralised databases progressed in 2025, including the transfer of ICT infrastructure to the Konza National Data Centre. • Capacity building was a core component of 2025 activities, specifically targeting knowledge gaps in modern networking and storage technologies. The ICT strategy includes a dedicated pillar for digital skills and innovation, ensuring that 2025 groundwork leads to a sustainable, longterm training program for ICT personnel.
Outcome 4.2: Efficient tools are used for statistics production and dissemination
• In 2025, the project defined requirements for a modern statistical toolkit via the draft ICT Strategy, prioritising automation across the data lifecycle, and incorporate alternative data sources like satellite imagery and web scraping. • A proposed KNBS Innovation Hub will pilot AI and Big Data to ensure long-term technical agility and reporting timeliness. • By establishing a roadmap for a formal Software Asset Management policy and centralised technical controls, the Bureau has moved toward a standardised digital environment model.
Component 5 The Kenya National Statistical System (NSS)
Outcome 5.1: KNBS supports and coordinates the Sector Statistics, i.e., the NSSs data producers
• In 2025, the KNBS continued its transition from a data producer to a functional system coordinator, fostering significant institutional self-sufficiency and internal ownership of the modernisation agenda. • The data science and training centre evolved into a hub for innovation in 2025, including the Young Statisticians Program. This permanent training facility demonstrates institutional commitment to continuous capacity building, serving both KNBS staff and NSS partners across the system. • Challenges includes financial dependency on external donors, rigid administrative patterns, such as inefficient personnel planning and per diem driven field work, and inconsistent momentum across decentralised sectors.
Outcome 5.2: KNBS provides guidelines and standards to the Sectors
• The revised Guidelines for Kenyan Official Statistics, adopted in 2024, was enforced during 2025 through sensitisation workshops for NSS members to ensure that the guidelines are applied throughout the system. • User-producer dialogues and a new digital feedback system were launched to ensure statistical production is demand driven and responsive to policymakers.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
